LESSON: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: DIALOGUES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we extract information from a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary from a text for information
2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension
3. appreciate the importance of reading indigenous texts for enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: DIALOGUES
This lesson teaches Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues for Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify vocabulary from a text for information
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
3. appreciate the importance of reading indigenous texts for enjoyment
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues above.
2. Explain Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we extract information from a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify vocabulary from a text for information
2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension
3. appreciate the importance of reading indigenous texts for enjoyment

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
